article_sentences: A 4.9-magnitude earthquake hit Uttarakhand’s Chamoli district at 10:23 pm on Tuesday, with tremors felt in Delhi and adjoining areas.
Tremors were felt in Delhi and adjoining areas late Tuesday after a 4.9-magnitude earthquake hit Uttarakhand's Chamoli district.
According to the National Center for Seismology (NCS) -- the nodal government agency monitoring earthquake activity -- the epicentre was located at a depth of 13 km in Uttarakhand's Chamoli.
The quake, which logged 4.9 magnitude on the Richter's scale, hit at 10:23 pm, the NCS added.

stories.headline: Jio taps stock markets for Rs30,200 crore in landmark IPO
stories.title: Jio taps stock markets for Rs30,200 crore in landmark IPO
stories.summary: As Jio Platforms heads to the stock markets to raise around Rs30,200 crore, the public offering marks more than just another large issue in India. It is a stock market debut of a digital service company which transformed India's telecom industry, accelerated the country's digital adoption and emerged as one of the most valuable businesses within the Reliance Industries ecosystem.Jio Platforms has formally kicked off its public market journey by filing its red herring prospectus, with the IPO scheduled to open on October 21 and close on October 23. The offering comprises a fresh issue of 27 crore shares. The Mukesh Ambani-led company aims to raise around Rs30,200 crore with a price band set at Rs1,065-1,119 per piece, positioning it among the biggest IPOs ever in India.Unlike most marquee IPOs, where early investors and promoters use the listing to partially monetise their holdings, Jio Platforms' Rs30,200-crore offering is an entirely fresh issue. Which means existing shareholders will not sell any shares through the IPO, instead the entire proceeds will be used by the company. A large part of the funds—up to Rs27,500 crore—will be used to pare debt at Reliance Jio Infocomm, while the balance will support general corporate requirements and future growth initiatives.Over the years, Jio Platforms has attracted an array of bluechip global investors, including Meta, Google, Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, KKR-backed Omicron Asia Holdings, General Atlantic Singapore, Abu Dhabi Investment Authority-backed Platinum Jasmine and TPG-managed India Markets. However, Reliance Industries continues to hold a controlling 66.43 percent stake in the company, retaining a firm grip over the group's most valuable digital asset.According to estimates by Bineet Banka and Abhishek Bhandari, analysts at Nomura, after the potential listing, Reliance’s 66.4 percent stake will be worth Rs481-506 per share which is 41 to 43 percent of the current share price. They say that the upper band of the issue price implies an equity valuation of Rs9.8-10.3 lakh crore.Also Read: Telecom tariffs back in focus as Airtel and Jio take divergent paths“Adding FY26 net debt of Rs1.4 lakh crore (including deferred spectrum liability of Rs1 lakh crore and lease liabilities), and netting the IPO cash, gives an enterprise value of Rs10.9-11.4 lakh crore,” Banka and Bhandari explain.The IPO offers investors a chance to participate in the growth of a business that serves hundreds of millions of users. Since its launch in 2016, Jio Platforms has transformed India's telecom landscape with ultra-cheap data plan, reshaped consumer behaviour and played a pivotal role in bringing millions of Indians online.“We believe that following its listing, Jio will likely need to demonstrate growth to public shareholders. And, with the period of easy subscriber gains likely ending, tariff hikes might become the primary driver of earnings growth,” Banka and Bhandari say.Also Read: Airtel turnaround: How Gopal Vittal rebuilt the telecom giantIndia's telecom sector is now largely a three-horse race between Reliance Jio, Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea. The industry's structure was fundamentally reshaped by Jio's entry in 2016, which triggered a brutal tariff war that led to consolidation and the exit of several operators. While Jio and Airtel have strengthened their market positions through scale, spectrum holdings and aggressive 5G rollouts, Vodafone Idea continues to battle a heavy debt burden, subscriber losses and the need for substantial capital expenditure to expand and upgrade its network.Meanwhile, Jio Platforms' proposed offering is set to become India's largest ever IPO, overtaking Hyundai Motor India's Rs27,800-crore issue in 2024. The rest in the pecking order are National Stock Exchange (Rs22,563 crore), LIC (Rs21,000-crore and Paytm (Rs18,300-crore).

opening: As Jio Platforms heads to the stock markets to raise around Rs30,200 crore, the public offering marks more than just another large issue in India.

It is a stock market debut of a digital service company which transformed India's telecom industry, accelerated the country's digital adoption and emerged as one of the most valuable businesses within the Reliance Industries ecosystem.
body: Jio Platforms has formally kicked off its public market journey by filing its red herring prospectus, with the IPO scheduled to open on October 21 and close on October 23.
The offering comprises a fresh issue of 27 crore shares.
The Mukesh Ambani-led company aims to raise around Rs30,200 crore with a price band set at Rs1,065-1,119 per piece, positioning it among the biggest IPOs ever in India.
Unlike most marquee IPOs, where early investors and promoters use the listing to partially monetise their holdings, Jio Platforms' Rs30,200-crore offering is an entirely fresh issue.
Which means existing shareholders will not sell any shares through the IPO, instead the entire proceeds will be used by the company.
A large part of the funds—up to Rs27,500 crore—will be used to pare debt at Reliance Jio Infocomm, while the balance will support general corporate requirements and future growth initiatives.

Over the years, Jio Platforms has attracted an array of bluechip global investors, including Meta, Google, Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, KKR-backed Omicron Asia Holdings, General Atlantic Singapore, Abu Dhabi Investment Authority-backed Platinum Jasmine and TPG-managed India Markets.
They say that the upper band of the issue price implies an equity valuation of Rs9.8-10.3 lakh crore.

“Adding FY26 net debt of Rs1.4 lakh crore (including deferred spectrum liability of Rs1 lakh crore and lease liabilities), and netting the IPO cash, gives an enterprise value of Rs10.9-11.4 lakh crore,” Banka and Bhandari explain.
The IPO offers investors a chance to participate in the growth of a business that serves hundreds of millions of users.

Since its launch in 2016, Jio Platforms has transformed India's telecom landscape with ultra-cheap data plan, reshaped consumer behaviour and played a pivotal role in bringing millions of Indians online.
“We believe that following its listing, Jio will likely need to demonstrate growth to public shareholders.
And, with the period of easy subscriber gains likely ending, tariff hikes might become the primary driver of earnings growth,” Banka and Bhandari say.
India's telecom sector is now largely a three-horse race between Reliance Jio, Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea.
The industry's structure was fundamentally reshaped by Jio's entry in 2016, which triggered a brutal tariff war that led to consolidation and the exit of several operators.

While Jio and Airtel have strengthened their market positions through scale, spectrum holdings and aggressive 5G rollouts, Vodafone Idea continues to battle a heavy debt burden, subscriber losses and the need for substantial capital expenditure to expand and upgrade its network.
Meanwhile, Jio Platforms' proposed offering is set to become India's largest ever IPO, overtaking Hyundai Motor India's Rs27,800-crore issue in 2024.
The rest in the pecking order are National Stock Exchange (Rs22,563 crore), LIC (Rs21,000-crore and Paytm (Rs18,300-crore).

stories.headline: India’s alternative-stay market set to grow 21 percent annually through FY29
stories.title: India’s alternative-stay market set to grow 21 percent annually through FY29
stories.summary: India’s alternative accommodation market is projected to grow at an annual rate of 21.2 percent through FY29. Rising tourism demand puts pressure on the country’s supply of rooms, thereby creating opportunities for homestays, villas and holiday homes.The segment’s gross booking value (GBV) is expected to rise to Rs415.1 billion in FY29, from Rs233.1 billion in FY26, according to How India Travels 2026, a report by online travel platform Booking.com and travel research and advisory firm VIDEC Consultants. Alternative accommodation accounted for around 13 percent of India’s lodging market by GBV in FY26, according to the report released on Thursday. The number of digitally distributed listings in the segment more than doubled, from 102,200 in FY23 to 215,000 in FY26.Travellers in India continue to make plans for October-December despite economic uncertainty, geopolitical tensions and higher airfares. But they are becoming more selective about where they go, how much they spend and how far in advance they book, says Laura Houldsworth, managing director for Asia-Pacific at Booking.com.Also Read: War, currency, fuel prices: Why summer holiday plans are shot“Uncertainty is a big driver. But also think that the desire to travel more frequently also leads into that,” Houldsworth tells Forbes India. Travellers planning one major holiday a year tend to book well in advance, she adds, while those taking several shorter breaks are more likely to plan spontaneously. “India has the shortest booking window globally.”A gap in accommodation supplyThe report found that the average booking window for alternative accommodation shortened from 15 days in FY23 to 12 days in FY26. Online searches for alternative accommodation grew 6 percent between FY24 and FY25, compared with 2 percent for hotels.At the report launch in New Delhi, Suman Billa, additional secretary and director general at the Ministry of Tourism, said the growth in tourism was putting pressure on the country’s existing accommodation capacity. “The demand is exploding, but the supply side is not keeping up,” he said. Citing the rise in domestic tourism visits and international tourist arrivals, Billa said even with new hotels in the pipeline, additional accommodation would be needed to meet demand. “There’s a big opportunity to bring homestays, bed and breakfasts, the alternative accommodation, to step into this gap.”Also Read: Gyms, myths, music: Skyscanner report highlights new travel trends among IndiansExpanding supply is not the only challenge. Billa pointed to inconsistent service standards at smaller properties, where the absence of staff can affect the guest experience. “One of the issues is, of course, standards of service delivery,” said Billa. “It doesn’t have the same backup systems as a hotel does.”Santosh Kumar, regional head, South Asia at Booking.com, said alternative accommodation was also helping spread tourism beyond established destinations. “It’s opening up a plethora of new destinations within the country. It’s helping balance tourism to a large extent, moving traffic away from our most commonly visited destinations,” he said.Also Read: Consumer brands moving into travelShorter booking windows, tighter budgetsThe growth in travel is taking place alongside pressure on household budgets. Airfares have risen ahead of the festive season as airlines contend with higher fuel costs and longer routes due to airspace restrictions amid the West Asia conflict. “Indians are definitely price sensitive. A few dollars can swing a decision for sure,” says Houldsworth.Flight and accommodation prices, however, do not always move in the same direction. Airlines typically offer lower fares earlier to fill seats, with prices rising as departure approaches. Hotels may lower rates closer to the date if rooms remain unoccupied. But for larger properties, such as villas or accommodation for an extended family, prices can rise as availability becomes limited.Booking.com’s search data suggests interest in travel remains strong ahead of the peak season. Searches for domestic accommodation for October-December were up 18 percent year-on-year, while those for international travel rose by 13 percent.“The opportunity to explore home countries is becoming more exciting, more interesting, because these alternative locations, alternative types of experiences are becoming more available,” she says.Houldsworth also points to better roads and increased domestic flight capacity as factors giving travellers more options for shorter trips. Domestic travel, she says, was growing faster than international travel.Beyond India, destinations across East and Southeast Asia are also attracting more travellers. “Intra-regional travel within Asia Pacific is the fastest-growing corridor globally,” Houldsworth says. Asked about the factors behind the shift towards Asia-Pacific, she says, “Cost is definitely an impact,” adding that economic conditions were challenging for many countries and travellers. Thailand, Vietnam and Indonesia are among the destinations benefiting from this shift.“Intergenerational travel is also very strong in Asia,” she says. “That also gives rise to staying, maybe not going too far, if you’re travelling with three generations and maybe 10-plus people.”

stories.headline: NITI Aayog Bats for Green Power Tariff, Open Access Rules for Data Centers
stories.title: NITI Aayog Bats for Green Power Tariff, Open Access Rules for Data Centers
stories.summary: Government thinktank NITI Aayog has urged the Ministry of Power and the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission to develop and publish model green tariff, banking, and open access principles for data centers’ procurement of round-the-clock renewable energy and battery storage-backed electricity. Data center operators must procure firm renewable power through captive generation or open access arrangements backed by energy storage systems so that the reliance on distribution companies’ electricity supply is reduced.

stories.title: Reliance Jio IPO to be listed soon: Why a 12% tariff hike may be coming in 3-4 months? Experts explain reasons
stories.summary: A Centrum report expects telecom tariffs to rise 12–15% over the next three to four months, citing limited competition and strong demand for 5G fixed wireless and broadband.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Amid growing buzz around Reliance Industries Limited-backed Jio Platforms’ initial public offerings, telecom users can see a 12% tariff hike over the coming three to four months.
The pricing environment has become favourable due to the presence of limited players in the industry.
Hence another 12-15% tariff hike is expected over next three to four months, according to a Centrum report.
Reliance Jio would continue to gain in the subscriber market share at the expense of Vodafone Idea Limited, according to Centrum experts.
Reliance Jio is likely to add 7 million subscribers on a sequential basis to 531 million.
Its Average Revenue Per User (ARPU) may grow by 1% QoQ to ₹216 per month.
The growth will be led by 5G FWW addition and higher number of days in the quarter.
The brokerage highlighted that the limited number of firms in the telecom industry has made the pricing environment more favourable.
“Reliance Jio and Airtel are also seeing strong traction in terms of 5G FWA and fixed broadband addition as penetration in the segment remains low.
The pricing environment has become more favourable with only 3+1 players and we expect another 12-15% tariff hike over next 3 to 4 months,” stated the report.
Tariff hikes are among the biggest growth levers for the Reliance Jio IPO.
The company has also said that its ARPU has significant headroom for growth.

stories.headline: Cabinet approves Integrated Transport & Logistics Authority for greater efficiency
stories.title: Cabinet approves Integrated Transport & Logistics Authority for greater efficiency
stories.summary: Seeks to address long-standing challenges; strengthen research, planning, appraisal, monitoring
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet approves' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Union Cabinet on Tuesday approved the setting up of a special purpose vehicle (SPV) — Integrated Transport & Logistics Authority (ITLA) - to strengthen research, planning, appraisal, monitoring and impact assessment of transportation and logistics.

“The approval seeks to address the long-standing challenges arising from fragmented planning and implementation across multiple transport-related Ministries and agencies,” per a statement issued by the government.

A long-term transport plan covering roads, railways, ports and shipping, civil aviation, inland waterways, coastal shipping, urban mobility and logistics, will be prepared by the ITLA, Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said at a media briefing following the Cabinet meeting.
The ITLA is expected to enhance the efficiency, sustainability and effectiveness of transport infrastructure development in India by fostering greater coordination and multi-modal integration.

“ITLA will prepare a comprehensive National Transport Master Plan with a planning horizon of ten years or more, covering roads, railways, ports and shipping, civil aviation, inland waterways, coastal shipping, urban mobility and logistics,” the statement highlighted.

It will evaluate short-term sectoral plans (five years or so) and annual plans of transport Ministries to ensure consistency and alignment with the National Transport Master Plan and promote multi-modal infrastructure development.

It will undertake technical appraisal of infrastructure projects of government, costing ₹500 crore or more, while financial appraisal will continue to be carried out through the existing financial appraisal mechanisms.

ITLA will also build a National Transport Data Repository, integrating datasets including GSTN e-way bills, FASTag, Vahan, GPS and urban traffic systems for freight-flow and origin-destination analytics.
It will advise on the review and updation of the National Logistics Policy, support capacity building, training and skilling, and promote research and innovation in transport and logistics.

The institution is expected to strengthen multimodal connectivity, improve infrastructure efficiency, reduce logistics costs and enhance India’s global logistics competitiveness as part of Vision 2047.

It will undertake technical appraisal of infrastructure projects of government, costing ₹500 crore or more, while financial appraisal will continue to be carried out through the existing financial appraisal mechanisms.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Flags AI-Generated Fake Judgments In Compilation Filed By Party
stories.title: Supreme Court Flags AI-Generated Fake Judgments In Compilation Filed By Party
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court has flagged an “undesirable incident” involving the alleged use of AI-generated, non-existent judgments in a compilation of cases submitted on behalf of the appellants, expressing concern over the conduct of the lawyers involved in the matter.
A Bench of Justice Dipankar Datta and Justice Augustine George Masih, while dismissing appeals filed by GSTAAD Hotels Pvt.
and Neo Capricorn Plaza Pvt.
against the initiation of insolvency proceedings against them, recorded that the respondents had immediately objected to the compilation, alleging that it contained judgments that did not exist.

“When queried by the Court, the Advocate-on-Record for the appellants sought to shift the entire blame on the appellants while at the same time feigning ignorance of what the compilation contained,” the Court observed.
The judgment further recorded that senior counsel appearing for the appellants subsequently took responsibility for the incident and sought forgiveness on behalf of the appellants.

The Court had initially considered imposing exemplary costs but, after being informed of the death of the first appellant, deleted the proposed costs and directed that there would be no order as to costs.

The Court made these observations while deciding appeals filed by the companies challenging the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal's decision upholding the admission of insolvency petitions under Section 7 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (IBC).

On the merits, the Supreme Court held that at the admission stage of an insolvency petition, a financial creditor is required to establish the occurrence of default through a summary assessment of documentary evidence and need not prove the exact outstanding liability after an exhaustive reconciliation of the corporate debtor's accounts.
“The trigger for initiation of the CIRP is the occurrence of a default, not the final adjudication of the creditor's entire claim,” the Court said.

The Bench clarified that disputes over the precise amount of outstanding debt, including the computation of interest, penal charges or other accounting entries, do not negate an established default or prevent admission of a Section 7 application, provided the statutory threshold under Section 4 of the IBC is satisfied.

“The standard applicable at the admission stage is one of preponderance of probabilities upon the documentary material placed on record,” the Court observed, adding that the threshold was deliberately modest and required a summary, prima facie finding of financial debt and default rather than a full trial into disputed facts.

stories.headline: RBI Was Mere Bystander When YES Bank Carried Out Business Clandestinely : Supreme Court
stories.title: RBI Was Mere Bystander When YES Bank Carried Out Business Clandestinely : Supreme Court
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court has observed that it would be “highly unfair” to make investors bear the consequences of administrative lapses, after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) allegedly allowed YES Bank's Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) ratio to fall to 0.6% despite earlier irregularities in the bank's functioning.
“The RBI was a mere bystander, allowing the CET1 ratio of YES BANK to drop to an astonishing low of 0.6% while the business of YES BANK was being carried out in a clandestine manner.
It cannot be denied that material irregularities in functioning of YES BANK were noticed much prior; criminal prosecution has also been initiated against the personnel of YES BANK.

However, to have the investors at the receiving end of the administrative lapses would be highly unfair.”, a bench of Justice Dipankar Datta and Justice Augustine George Masih observed while setting aside the write-down of ₹8,415 crore worth of Additional Tier 1 (AT-1) bonds.
The Court upheld the Bombay High Court's decision, holding that YES Bank's Administrator lacked the authority to write down the bonds after the final reconstruction scheme came into force.
“…administrator appointed under the BR Act has to act squarely within the four corners of the powers conferred upon him under the statute.
He acts as a substitute for the Board of Directors, to run the company in an efficient manner.

Any act performed by the administrator beyond the powers clothed upon him would be wholly illegal and void.”, the Court said, emphasizing that an Administrator cannot be said to have exercised the power vested in the RBI.
The Court noted that material irregularities in YES Bank's functioning had been noticed much earlier and criminal prosecution had also been initiated against bank personnel.
However, it said investors could not be made to bear the consequences of administrative failures.
Although the draft reconstruction scheme expressly provided for a permanent write-down of AT-1 bonds, the clause was omitted from the final scheme notified on March 13, 2020.
The Administrator nevertheless wrote down the bonds the next day, extinguishing investors' claims.

article_sentences: The annual family income limit criterion for financial assistance from the Kerala Chief Minister’s Distress Relief Fund (CMDRF) will be increased from ₹2 lakh to ₹3 lakh.
The decision was taken in the weekly Cabinet meeting held on Wednesday, Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan said here on Thursday.
The Cabinet has also increased the CMDRF amounts that can be sanctioned at various levels.
At the Chief Minister’s level, the amount has been increased from ₹3 to ₹5 lakh, and up to ₹1 lakh at the Revenue Minister’s level.
The Special Secretary (Revenue) can sanction up to ₹50,000, and the district collectors, ₹25,000.
Further, the Cabinet also decided to constitute an untied fund of ₹1 crore for district collectors to use in emergencies.
The Cabinet has given its approval for the Draft Kerala State Data Policy 2026.
The policy covers aspects such as creation of data, safe and controlled data sharing, its quality and compatibility.
The need for a policy arose from a need for a technical mechanism for data sharing among government departments, the Chief Minister said.
The draft policy was prepared by the Kerala State.

stories.headline: Ranji Trophy 2026-27: Defending champion J&K begins title defence against Madhya Pradesh
stories.title: Ranji Trophy 2026-27: Defending champion J&K begins title defence against Madhya Pradesh
stories.summary: Jammu and Kashmir’s strengths and vulnerabilities were on display in its Irani Cup 2026 defeat, but it will be bolstered by the return of Auqib Nabi fresh off his debut for the national team.
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: A week after the Irani Cup defeat exposed the cracks in its armour, Jammu and Kashmir gets a chance to reset on familiar turf.
The defending champion begins its Ranji Trophy campaign against Madhya Pradesh at the Sher-i-Kashmir Stadium on Sunday, hoping to leave that disappointment behind and find its feet again.
India pacer Auqib Nabi’s availability offers a timely boost, although J&K has rested Umar Nazir, who claimed six wickets in the Irani Cup.
Nasir Lone and Sunil Kumar provide further pace options, while Umran Malik, despite being with the squad, has not been considered.
The bigger concern, however, is the batting.
J&K squandered a first-innings lead against Rest of India before collapsing in the second innings.
Shubham Khajuria, Qamran Iqbal, Abdul Samad and captain Paras Dogra will need to shoulder the responsibility if the host is to make its home advantage count.
Building partnerships and avoiding another collapse will be central to its plans.
Madhya Pradesh, meanwhile, has spent the past week in Srinagar acclimatising to the conditions and arrives without any injury concerns.
Led by Shubham Sharma, it will miss Rajat Patidar and Venkatesh Iyer but retains considerable batting depth through Yash Dubey, Harsh Gawli and Himanshu Mantri.
The bowling attack, spearheaded by the experienced Avesh Khan and featuring Kuldeep Sen, has the pace to trouble the hosts.
Saransh Jain and Kumar Kartikeya add experience to the spin department, giving MP a balanced attack.

stories.headline: India’s new GDP methodology a welcome development: IMF
stories.title: India’s new GDP methodology a welcome development: IMF
stories.summary: New methodology aligns with good practices, says IMF official
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Washington: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) on Thursday endorsed India's updated gross domestic product (GDP) calculation methodology, describing the base revision as a "welcome development" consistent with its advice.
Krishna Srinivasan, Director of the IMF's Asia and Pacific Department, said the revisions aligned with recommendations from the Fund's statistics department.
"These revisions to the methodology are entirely consistent with what the advice we've been giving them, including from our statistics department," he said.
Srinivasan noted that India had also issued an explanatory note on the changes.
While there was room for further improvement, he acknowledged the work done by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) to improve GDP statistics.
The IMF official also said India had faced the energy shock with strong economic fundamentals and responded well.
Pressure on the rupee should not be interpreted as a sign of economic failure, he said, attributing exchange-rate movements to global interest rates, investor risk appetite and oil prices.
The IMF's Regional Economic Outlook for Asia and the Pacific, released on Thursday, identified India among emerging economies whose currencies came under pressure following the energy shock.
It said the pressure had partly eased in recent months and noted that India was among countries that intervened in foreign exchange markets.
The endorsement comes amid a political controversy over India's reported GDP growth of 7.8 per cent in the June quarter.
Former Finance Secretary S C Garg had questioned the figures, alleging that growth was artificially boosted by compressing the previous year's data.
Opposition parties also questioned the credibility of the statistics.
